target_customer: Homeowner associations (comunidades de propietarios) in Spain that pay a property administrator
problem: Traditional property administrators (administradores de fincas) are slow, opaque and manual. Aldara automates back office operations with in-house AI and offers online voting and a real-time community portal.
business_model: Management fee per community as a tech-enabled HOA administrator

founders.name: Daniel Carmona
education: Aerospace engineer (per YC page, no school named)
previous_startups: Software import business with 15M in annual sales (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page and Spanish press name him CEO.

founders.name: Dani Torramilans
founders.background_notes: Named CTO by the YC launch post and El Derecho.

founders.name: Miquel Llobet
founders.background_notes: YC company page lists him as co-founder with Product Manager at Google and first APM at Skyscanner; the launch post names only two founders, so his role at Aldara is unclear.

technical_complexity.rationale: Online voting, a resident portal and workflow automation are standard software; the operating complexity is regulatory and service delivery, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Service heavy administration with local licensing norms; software features are copyable and no network effect is described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent administrators were fragmented small offices; no source shows them copying Aldara.

market_need_then: Spanish press describes owners who cannot attend meetings in person and want online voting and transparent communication, which Aldara pitched. No spend data found.

branding.domain_note: Uses aldara.com per the YC page; acquisition details not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Modern, agile, transparent administration pitch in Spanish press

brand_strength.rationale: Several Spanish outlets covered the funding round and the launch, but no brand specific story or community was found.

outcome_analysis: Aldara is a Barcelona HOA administrator that replaces manual back office work with automation and raised a reported 2.7 million euro round in early 2024 led by Y Combinator and Kfund. The YC page marks it Inactive while Spanish press and a YC mirror show it active, and one unverified page claims an acquisition, so the real outcome is unclear and no failure cause is public.
notes: Round is EUR 2.7M (amount_usd left null, no USD figure sourced). Date: Seedtable says February 2024, its URL says 2024-01; recorded as 2024-01. The El Referente article returned 403 so it was not opened; capital-riesgo and Seedtable were from search results. Status conflict: the YC page fetched says Inactive, a search summary said YC lists Active; a Nordic9 page headlined acquired (2026-02-26) was unverifiable and is not recorded as an exit. Company site aldara.com did not resolve. Founders' schools not found. Daniel Carmona is called the CEO in sources while the YC page profile text did not map names to roles. Competitors: no source dated near mid 2022 found (results were 2024 to 2026), so the list is empty.
